newsitem.title: FRANCE: Children, pregnant woman slain in Algeria -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Children, pregnant woman slain in Algeria -- paper.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists, in latest reported massacres in Algeria, killed 26 people including six children and a pregnant woman, the country's main Arabic language newspaper said on Thursday.

The killings, reported by Al Khabar, underscored the pitiless conflict still shaking the North African country despite its focus on political events following the June 5 general election which President Liamine Zeroual hopes will help end the violence.
Al Khabar said 11 died in one attack and 15 in the second.
Another newspaper, the independent El Watan, also reported the massacre of the 15 who died, in Jaouaza village, near Lardjem, Tissemsilt province.
There was no official confirmation of the killings.

But diplomats say the fact two of the main newspapers reported them is effective confirmation, in the light of the authorities' huge powers to act against newspapers which carry security reports which the authorities may challenge.
Al Khabar said a group of "terrorists" -- Algerian shorthand for Moslem fundamentalists -- attacked the isolated Jaouaza village in the Ouarsenis mountain range early on Tuesday.

They arrived at 4 a.m. and tried to force the women to leave the village with them. When they refused, 15 of the inhabitants were killed. Among them were six children and three women, one of whom was pregnant.
Al Khabar said that earlier in the week, another group killed 11 people in a village 50 km (30 miles) from Bechar, a provincial capital about 775 km (480 miles) southwest of Algiers.
The newspaper also said security forces had wiped out 10 "terrorists" in a search operation over four days this week in the western Tlemcen area.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria since early 1992 when violence erupted after the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by Islamic fundamentalists.

Algeria earlier this month held fresh general elections which were dominated by a pro-Zeroual party, which took 156 seats in the 380-seat assembly, although two legal Islamist-leaning parties won a total of 103.
Zeroual has reappointed outgoing prime minister Ahmed Ouyahia to form a new government.
Since last Saturday, Algerian newspapers have reported at least three other massacres, including one of five members of the same family who had their throats cut in a house in the Algerian capital.

In one of the other attacks, according to El Watan 13 people died in Douaouada village in the western coastal province of Tipaza. Eight were burnt alive and five had their throats cut -- the oldest being 75 and the youngest a baby girl of two.
More than 90 villagers were slaughtered by Moslem guerrillas last month in the worst massacre in the five-and-a-half years of violence.
